Good evening everyone, and thanks for coming out. Just a few quick things before we start. The talk tonight runs about fifty minutes and we will take questions for fifteen after that, so we should all be out by nine. If you signed up for the reading group, we have moved it from Wednesday to Thursday, same time, same room, starting next week. There are still four places. Coffee is at the back and it is free tonight. And if anyone finds a grey umbrella, it belongs to the gentleman in the second row, and he has already asked me twice.

Here is a drill you can do in four minutes a day, and it is more useful than any app. Take one minute of audio, anything with a transcript, and listen to it three times. The first time, do not read, and do not try to catch every word. Write down only the words you are certain about, even if there are five of them. The second time, still without the text, fill in what you can around those five. Only on the third pass do you open the transcript, and when you do, look for the gaps you left and ask what happened in them. You will find the same two or three things happening over and over. Learn those, and the speed problem quietly becomes a smaller problem.
